overview: In the Signature teaching of indoor plants basics, Current Research Frontiers in Indoor Plants Basics is a load-bearing idea: understand it and much of the field clicks into place. Drainage means pots must drain; sitting in water rots roots Fertilizer means half-strength in growing season, none in winter Together these ideas give the learner working intuition, not just vocabulary. The Signature presentation stresses why each principle holds, shows where it is used in real practice, and connects it forward to the Advanced material that follows.
core_concepts: Drainage: pots must drain; sitting in water rots roots
Fertilizer: half-strength in growing season, none in winter
key_laws: More houseplants die of overwatering than underwatering.
Match the plant to your light, not your wish.
vocabulary: Bright indirect: strong light without direct sunbeams
Leggy: stretched pale growth from too little light
methods: Water method: check the top inch; if dry, water until it drains, empty the saucer
history: Houseplants boomed in Victorian ferneries and again in the 1970s; the 2010s brought a new wave with monsteras and fiddle-leaf figs.
key_points: Drainage: pots must drain; sitting in water rots roots
